status: ADVISORY — the governing rule is unchanged and no case was altered
the_governing_rule: Group SUPPORTED cases by canonical gold evidence-span set; any group larger than one is an evidence collision. That rule is the coordinator's and is applied as written.
the_observation: Exact-span grouping under-detects capability duplication when the retrieval unit is a chunk rather than a span. Two cases can carry different gold spans that fall inside the SAME cs_v1_control chunk. A system retrieving that one chunk is then credited on both cases, which is the outcome the collision rule exists to prevent.

detail.note: three cases, one chunk. A16 has a DIFFERENT span from A09/A10 and is invisible to exact-span grouping.
three cases, one chunk, three distinct spans.

measured_at_50_adjudicated.ratio: 4x more chunk-level groups than exact-span groups, and 9 cases involved rather than 2

why_this_is_not_a_unilateral_rule_change: Which unit counts as duplication is a benchmark-design decision with real trade-offs, and it is the coordinator's to make. Span-level grouping is defensible: two questions can legitimately probe different facts that a chunker happened to place together, and the chunk boundary is a property of cs_v1_control rather than of the questions. Chunk-level grouping is also defensible: it matches what a retrieval system is actually scored on. Nothing here resolves that, and no case has been deleted, merged, or reweighted.
options_for_the_coordinator: Keep exact-span grouping as the sole gate. Chunk overlap is then accepted as within-benchmark redundancy.
Keep exact-span grouping as the gate but cap how many accepted cases may share one chunk.
Add chunk-set grouping as a second gate, adjudicated the same way — explicit ruling per group, never resolved by system performance.
Defer until all 150 are adjudicated, then decide against the full picture. The counts above will change.
caveats: Computed over 50 of 150 adjudicated cases; the final numbers will differ.

Chunk membership is specific to chunk_set cs_v1_control on snapshot snap_689e336380a054d8039dc35b2c09cd0a. A different chunker would give different groups, which is itself an argument for treating span-level as the stable unit.
A span overlapping a chunk boundary maps to every chunk it touches; the overlap test used here is interval intersection, not containment.
constraints_honored: No case deleted, merged, or reweighted.
No retrieval or reranking system consulted — chunk membership comes from the frozen chunk table, not from any system's output.
The final collision gate remains unrun until all 150 are adjudicated.
